celery_tasks.does: Recount the last days from scheduling's tables and report any drift from analytics_daily (reports; never overwrites)
celery_tasks.name: analytics.reconcile

celery_tasks.does: Extract the text of an uploaded report (PDF) for review
celery_tasks.name: clinical.extract_document

celery_tasks.does: Daily: delete outbox rows published more than a week ago. Unpublished rows are never touched, however old -- they are the backlog.
celery_tasks.name: events.purge_published

celery_tasks.does: Every minute: queued rows whose enqueue was lost (the process died between commit and enqueue), and claims whose worker died. `claim` keeps a double send impossible.
celery_tasks.name: notifications.requeue_stuck

celery_tasks.does: Send one notification: claim the row, throttle per patient in Redis, email (Mailpit) or SMS, retry with backoff, dead-letter
celery_tasks.name: notifications.send

celery_tasks.does: Fail bookings stuck in pending whose workflow is gone: free the slot, release the payment hold
celery_tasks.name: scheduling.reconcile_stale_pending

consumers.does: Adds each booking, cancellation, no-show and completed visit to the day's counts in analytics_daily
consumers.name: analytics.daily-rollup

consumers.does: Turns events a patient should hear about into one notification row each, sent by Celery after commit
consumers.name: notifications.patient-messages

consumers.does: Starts CancelFollowUpWorkflow: stop the visit timer, refund, offer the slot to the waitlist
consumers.name: scheduling.cancel-follow-up

consumers.does: Starts PostVisitWorkflow: capture the booking's payment
consumers.name: scheduling.post-visit

consumers.does: Starts ProviderDeactivationWorkflow when a provider goes inactive: cancel their future appointments
consumers.name: scheduling.provider-deactivation

consumers.does: Keeps the knowledge service's own provider directory and indexes each active provider into Qdrant
consumers.name: knowledge.provider-directory

consumers.does: Fills the assistant's deny-list: tokens issued before a revocation are refused
consumers.name: assistant.revocations

consumers.does: Records every booking with its origin (assistant or not) for the conversion rate
consumers.name: assistant.conversions

temporal_workflows.does: Booking: create pending, validate, claim the slot, billing pre-check, schedule reminders, confirm last; compensate on failure
temporal_workflows.name: BookAppointmentWorkflow

temporal_workflows.does: Readiness probe: proves a worker is polling and executing
temporal_workflows.name: CanaryWorkflow

temporal_workflows.does: What must eventually follow a cancellation that is already committed: stop the visit timer, refund, and offer the freed slot to the waitlist. Started best-effort after the cancel's own transaction (spec §4.3), so none of it can fail or delay the cancel.
temporal_workflows.name: CancelFollowUpWorkflow

temporal_workflows.does: What follows a completed visit (Week 3 slice 4; PART-A-FR-3): capture the booking's authorisation. Started by the `visits.completed` consumer under `post-visit-<visit_id>`, so a redelivered event cannot charge twice -- and the capture is idempotent besides. The follow-up reminder joins this workflow in slice 5.
temporal_workflows.name: PostVisitWorkflow

temporal_workflows.does: A provider went inactive: cancel each of their future appointments (PRD R-25, spec D-23). Started by the `providers.state` consumer. Each cancel is the ordinary paired write, so each one emits `appointments.cancelled`, and that event's consumer does the rest -- the refund, the waitlist, and (slice 5) telling the patient.
temporal_workflows.name: ProviderDeactivationWorkflow

temporal_workflows.does: Book the new slot first, release the old one only if that confirmed (D-14): a failed reschedule leaves the patient with the appointment they had.
temporal_workflows.name: RescheduleWorkflow

temporal_workflows.does: The no-show timer for one confirmed appointment (spec D-12, §4.2).
temporal_workflows.name: VisitWorkflow
